title: Snickerdoodles
summary: Soft, crackle-topped butter cookies rolled in cinnamon sweetener, with cream of tartar for their signature tang.
steps: Beat the butter and erythritol until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt, and stir into the butter mixture to a soft dough. Chill 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Mix the coating erythritol and cinnamon in a small bowl.
Roll the dough into 16 balls, roll each in the cinnamon mixture and set 5 cm (2 in) apart. Press each down to about 1.5 cm (½ in) thick, since almond-flour dough does not spread much.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until the tops crackle and the edges just colour. Cool on the sheet 10 minutes.
dairy_free_notes: With dairy-free butter the cookies are a touch softer and flatter; flatten them a little less before baking.
tips: Cream of tartar gives the tang; don't replace it with extra baking powder.

origin.history: Snickerdoodles appear in American cookbooks in the late nineteenth century and are often associated with New England baking. The origin of the name is uncertain: it is sometimes linked to the German Schneckennudeln, a kind of cinnamon roll, but that connection is a guess rather than a documented fact.
